rddid

Estimation and inference for regression-discontinuity difference-in-discontinuities (RD-DID) designs, where a confounding policy switches at the same cutoff as the treatment of interest. Implements the framework of Leventer and Nevo.

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05847

The data are long, one row per unit-period, with an outcome, a running variable, a period and (for a panel) a unit id. Periods are of two kinds: in the RD period the treatment of interest switches at the cutoff; in a comparison period it does not, while the confounding policy switches in every period. rddid() nets the comparison-period discontinuities out of the RD-period one. When the running variable varies over time within a unit, four validation tests (rd_typecont(), rd_compstable(), rd_homog(), rd_trendcell()) check the identifying assumptions of Section 4 of the paper.

Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("dorleventer/rddid")

Quick start

Below, periods 1 and 2 are comparison periods (the confounding discontinuity is 1 in both) and period 3 is the RD period, where the treatment of interest adds 1 at the cutoff.

library(rddid)

set.seed(1)
n <- 2000
R <- runif(n, -1, 1)                 # time-invariant running variable, cutoff at 0
u <- rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)                # unit effect
dat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(t) {
  V <- as.integer(R >= 0)            # confounding treatment: sharp RD in every period
  W <- V * (t == 3)                  # treatment of interest: sharp RD in period 3 only
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), t = t, R = R,
             Y = R + R^2 * (R >= 0) + 1 * V + 1 * W + u + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5))
}))

rddid(dat, y = "Y", x = "R", time = "t", id = "id",
      t_rd = 3, comparisons = c(1, 2), weights = "constant")
#> RD-DID estimate of ATT(t_RD)
#>   RD period: 3   comparison periods: 1, 2
#>   weights: constant [0.5, 0.5]
#>   bwselect: iter  (5 iterations)
#>   scheme: pc (auto-detected)
#> 
#>                    Estimate   Std.Err.   95% CI
#>   Conventional      1.09413    0.09746   [  0.90312,   1.28514]
#>   Robust            1.12176    0.11715   [  0.89215,   1.35138]
#> 
#>   Robust SE by scheme: cs=0.18902  pc=0.11715  pv=0.11715
